title: A closed map lifts specializations
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces and let $g:X\to Y$ be a map such that $g(C)$ is closed in $Y$ for every closed subset $C\subseteq X$ (this is the definition of a closed map; continuity is not needed). For points $a,b$ in a topological space, say that $a$ specializes to $b$ when $b\in\overline{\{a\}}$. If $x\in X$ and $g(x)$ specializes to $y\in Y$, then there exists $x'\in X$ such that $x$ specializes to $x'$ and $g(x')=y$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0066 (label lemma-closed-open-map-specialization), part (1): if f is closed then specializations lift along f.
